tier_reason: The README Performance section runs foldhash against SipHash-1-3 (std::hash::RandomState) plus aHash and fxhash. The code is public in benches/bench.rs (criterion), with tools/extract-bench-results.py and tools/format-bench-results.py for the tables. The README states stable Rust 1.80.1, runs with and without -C target-cpu=native, and the CPUs (2023 Apple M2, Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C). The Xeon 8481c geometric mean is 6.21 for foldhash-f vs 28.70 for siphash, exactly as in the record.
notes: Numbers verified. SipHash-1-3 is last on almost every row (avg_rank 4.97 of 5); units are ns per op. Other geometric means: 6.00 vs 29.49 on Xeon with native, 4.41 vs 21.94 on M2. The record's last_commit (2026-07-03) is the repo's pushed_at; the newest commit on master is 2026-06-29. The current bench.rs has since added rapidhash, so the code has moved on from the README run.

tier_reason: The benchmark code is public: rapidhash-bench/benches/bench/basic.rs (twox_hash::XxHash64 and XxHash3_64, and the wyhash crate), realworld/main.rs, docs/run_benchmarks.sh and docs/generate_charts.py. Flags are stated: the workspace [profile.bench] sets opt-level=3, lto=fat and codegen-units=1, and native runs add RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native. The CPUs are named. No rustc version is stated anywhere in the repo, so this is first-party with partial methodology: C, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'significant throughput improvement over wyhash and foldhash'; 'places second to gxhash on some benchmarks'. Raw-throughput charts, derived from page data (SVG chart geometry), Xeon 8488c portable: u64 ~1166 M items/s rapidhash-f vs ~1133 wyhash, ~739 xxhash64, ~48 xxhash3_64 (Hasher trait). 4 KB: ~30.5 vs ~25.0 GB/s (xxhash3_64). 64 KB: ~31.6 vs ~32.2 GB/s (xxhash3_64 slightly ahead), ~15.0 xxhash64, ~19.3 wyhash. On AMD EPYC 9R14, xxhash3_64 beats rapidhash-f from 4 KB up (~36.4 vs ~30.1 GB/s at 4 KB; ~51.4 vs ~31.1 GB/s at 64 KB). Rapidhash leads xxhash3_64 on M1 Max at 64 KB (~45.9 vs ~36.8 GB/s) and beats xxhash64 and wyhash everywhere.
corrections.baseline: xxHash (XXH64, XXH3-64, via the Rust twox-hash 2.1.1 crate) and wyhash (Rust wyhash crate 0.6.0)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc (version not stated) via cargo criterion; workspace [profile.bench] opt-level=3, lto="fat", codegen-units=1, incremental=false; portable runs without RUSTFLAGS, native runs with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" (docs/run_benchmarks.sh)
corrections.workload: Raw hashing throughput vs input size (2 B to 4 KB, 64 KB, u64) across rapidhash-f/q, xxhash3_64, xxhash64, wyhash, foldhash, metrohash, rustc-hash, ahash, t1ha, farmhash, seahash, highwayhash, fxhash, SipHash default and gxhash (native only), all through std::hash::BuildHasher/Hasher. Plus the foldhash suite (hashonly/lookupmiss/lookuphit/setbuild on u32/u64/pairs/ipv4/ipv6/strings/accesslog/kilobyte blobs) vs foldhash/fxhash/ahash/siphash/gxhash.
corrections.caveats: The linked .txt tables only compare against foldhash/fxhash/ahash/siphash; the xxHash and wyhash comparison is only in the SVG charts. The baselines are Rust ports (twox-hash, wyhash crate), not reference C xxHash. XXH3 is driven through the streaming Hasher trait, which inflates its small-input cost. XXH3 matches or beats rapidhash on large inputs on x86 (EPYC 9R14 from 4 KB up; Xeon 8488c at 64 KB). No rustc version is stated. Crate is dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 (GitHub shows only Apache-2.0).

notes: The original benchmark_url (Xeon 8488c .txt) has no xxHash or wyhash column. The corrected URL (the matching SVG) does compare against them, so page_compares_against_baseline is judged on the SVG. The SVG has no <text> glyphs; I read the values from the matplotlib bar/line geometry against the axis ticks, so they are approximate. 'Beats xxhash64/xxhash3_64' is overstated: it holds for small and medium inputs and for xxhash64, but XXH3 wins on large inputs on AMD. Stars 278 and the Fuchsia/Turso/metrics/alloy users are confirmed on the README.

tier_reason: The readme's charts compare rapidhash against native C XXH3 and Unity.Collections' Burst xxHash3 on a Ryzen 5950X and an M4 Max. The Burst side's harness is public (Assets/HashBenchmark.cs), and VS 2022 17.14.23, Xcode 16.1 and the Unity 2022.3/6.3 versions are named. No compile flags are given, for either the native build or the Burst/editor settings. The native numbers come from the upstream Nicoshev/rapidhash bench program, which is not in this repo. First-party with partial methodology: C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Readme text: rapidhash reaches about 38 GB/s on Ryzen 5950X and about 67 GB/s on Apple M4 Max; 'Rapidhash is always faster than xxhash (XXH3)'. Read from the readme chart images (approximate): Ryzen 5950X plateau, Burst rapidhash ~38 GB/s vs Burst XXH3 ~23.5-24.5 GB/s; native XXH3 ~37.5-38 GB/s, about equal to rapidhash from 16 KB up. M4 Max: native rapidhash ~68-73 GB/s, Burst rapidhash ~63-68 GB/s, native XXH3 ~49-50 GB/s, Burst XXH3 ~28-29 GB/s.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Native C (upstream rapidhash/xxhash bench program): Visual Studio 2022 (17.14.23) on Windows, Xcode 16.1 on macOS, flags not stated. C# port: Unity 2022.3 (ProjectVersion 2022.3.62f3) and Unity 6.3, Burst (1.8.23 in packages-lock.json), run in the editor from a non-Burst C# script; Burst options not stated.
corrections.caveats: Small single-purpose port (17 stars; all 8 commits on 2026-03-07); the readme does not say it is finished. The harness is a plain C# editor script that the author notes may add overhead. The Burst-vs-Burst gap partly reflects Unity.Collections' XXH3 port, which the author says is 30-40% slower than native C XXH3. Against native XXH3 on the Ryzen 5950X, rapidhash only ties at 16 KB and above, and native XXH3 is slightly ahead at 32-128 MB, despite the 'always faster' line. The native harness is not in this repo.

notes: Only the 38 and 67 GB/s figures are in the readme text; every XXH3 value comes from the two chart PNGs, which I opened and read. maintenance_status changed from 'finished' to 'active': the last commit is 2026-03-07 (under 12 months old) and I found no completion statement. License MIT (LICENSE file, spdx MIT) is confirmed.
